group:paper-mock-shandong-zibo-2026-05-s.overview: 文章介绍布达佩斯图书馆每月一次的讲座：青少年教老年人数字技能。64岁的基什借此学会用翻译工具上网；项目弥合数字鸿沟，青少年也收获耐心和对旧时代的了解，两代人建立起真正的联系。
group:paper-mock-shandong-zibo-2026-05-s.fullTranslationZh:
在布达佩斯一个寒冷的下午，64岁的焦尔吉·佩蒂克·基什急切地赶往图书馆。她去那里不是为了看书，而是去参加 Netrevalók——一个每月举办的讲座，老年人在这里跟青少年学习数字技能。
基什曾在昏迷状态中度过了四年，她迫切需要脑力上的刺激。然而，由于不懂英语，她缺乏独自上网的信心。“我以前都不敢乱点东西。万一我弄砸了怎么办？”通过这个项目，她学会了使用微软翻译——这个“新工具”帮助她不再那么与外界脱节。
这个项目弥合了日益扩大的数字鸿沟。在匈牙利，15至50岁的人中有97%使用互联网，而80岁以上的老人中有90%不上网。许多老年人连基本操作都很吃力。正如图书馆馆长所指出的：“对老年人来说，数字化实际上把他们排除在外了。”受益是双向的。青少年志愿者收获了耐心，也得以了解数字时代之前的世界。“和他们聊天就像回到了过去。”19岁的萨吉·弗鲁赫特说。这段经历激励他设计更便于使用的技术。
对基什这样的参与者来说，这些讲座提供的不只是技能。他们不仅学会了在数字世界中畅行，还与年轻一代建立起有意义的联系。这座跨越技术鸿沟、简单却有力的桥梁提醒我们：真正的联结取决于耐心、理解以及彼此学习的共同意愿——用真正重要的技能把两代人的世界连在一起。

completedSourceTexts.text: On a cold Budapest afternoon, 64-year-old Györgyi Petik Kis eagerly hurries to the library. She isn’t there to read, but to attend Netrevalók – monthly lectures where seniors learn digital skills from teenagers.

Kis, who spent four years in a state of unconsciousness, desperately needs mental stimulation. However, without English skills, she lacks confidence to navigate the internet on her own. “I was afraid to click on things. What if I messed up?” Through the program, she has learned to use Microsoft Translate – a “new tool” helping her feel less disconnected.

The program bridges a growing digital divide. While 97% of Hungarians aged 15-50 use the internet, 90% of those over 80 do not go online. Many seniors struggle with basic tasks. As the library director points out, “For the elderly, going digital actually leaves them out.” The benefits extend both ways. Teen volunteers gain patience and insights into a pre-digital world. “Talking to them is like going back in time,” says 19-year-old Sagie Fruchter. The experience inspires him to design more accessible technology.

For participants like Kis, the lectures offer more than skills. They not only learn to navigate the digital world but also build meaningful connections with younger generations. This simple yet powerful bridge across the technological divide serves as a reminder that genuine connection depends on patience, understanding, and a mutual willingness to learn from one another – using the skills that truly matter to bring their worlds together.
